audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows sat off the packet chart and off their own prose: Level 1 read Skill while whys[0] says Gnar outranges everything you have; First item and 2+ items read Gnar while whys[5] and whys[6] both describe Maokai winning the attrition.
audit.why: Gnar's mini-form poke owns the opener outright, and the lane inverts once Maokai has HP and resistances — the packet chart (Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Maokai/Maokai) already said so, and the mirror audit flipped exactly these three rows to it.
audit.corrected: Level 1 to Gnar at 4/10, First item to Maokai at 6/10, 2+ items to Maokai at 7/10, proposed as matched full+content pairs. Ratings are the inverse of the mirror's 6/10, 4/10 and 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and 2-item phase whys were generic boilerplate that named no spike at all.
audit.why: The lane's whole shape is that Gnar front-loads and Maokai back-loads; the spike rows are where that has to be said.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten around Heartsteel plus Sap Magic outlasting mini-form poke, keyed to catching him on an empty Rage bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says in three places that Gnar's hop outranges Twisted Advance ('boomerang (Q) and hop (E) both outrange your W'). Hop is 475 range; Twisted Advance is 525. His hop does not outrange the W — it lands him inside it. Only Boomerang Throw, at 1100, genuinely outranges you.
audit.why: This flips the single most important decision in the lane. A Gnar who hops at you is in root range, which is the one moment a Maokai gets in the first three levels; the page currently tells the player that moment does not exist.
audit.corrected: Corrected in early, spikes[0].text and whys[1], each stating the real 1100 / 525 / 475 numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight, and nothing said Sap Magic's heal cooldown drops when an enemy spell strikes Maokai.
audit.why: Together they mean Gnar cannot answer the engage itself — anything thrown into the dash whiffs — and that his boomerang poke is partly paying for the heal that undoes it. The mirror audit flagged the same two facts as its headline finds.
audit.corrected: Untargetability written into mid; the Sap Magic mechanic written into mid and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects is right that there is no cooldown sequencing anywhere. breakdown.cooldowns tells the player to 'track GNAR!' as if it were the gating cooldown.
audit.why: GNAR! is not what gates Mega form — the Rage bar is, and Rage is generated by being in combat, not by a timer. Meanwhile the real numbers matter: GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 but 30s at rank 3, and Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 with the cooldown cut when he catches it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten to track the Rage bar and to carry the 90s/30s and 16s figures.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Gnar contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw is 1100 range and costs nothing — at level 1 you have one ability and no answer. Concede CS rather than walk in.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on GNAR!'s cooldown.
edits.after: First item is yours — Heartsteel and Sap Magic outlast his poke. Force it on empty Rage.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gnar carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on you win the grind: root chains and Sap Magic beat mini-form kiting. Catch him in mini with no Rage and he dies.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. W-peel/dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gnar's Rage bar, not a cooldown, is what you track: it decides whether you face mini or Mega. Engage on empty. - GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 but only 30s at rank 3. - Boomerang Throw 16s, and catching it cuts that.

edits.before: He keeps hopping (E) and throwing boomerang (Q) while your W (Twisted Advance) still can't reach the gap he opens — he chips you for free.
edits.after: He throws Boomerang Throw from 1100 and resets distance with Hop, and one point in W (Twisted Advance) will not let me repeat a trade.

edits.before: Mini-Gnar's boomerang (Q) and hop (E) outrange your W, so he chips you for free before you can step up and lock him.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against your 525 W, so mini-Gnar chips you for free before you can step up and lock him.

edits.before: Gnar owns the first three levels here and you have to respect it. His mini-form boomerang (Q) and hop (E) both outrange your W (Twisted Advance), so he chips you for free while you have nothing to answer with — at Level 1 you only have one ability and no combo. Don't walk into his Q range trying to last-hit with melee swings; eat the minor CS loss and wait. Your one real opening is once you complete W+Q+E around Levels 2-3: if he hops in or stands still to throw, W onto him, Q-knockback, and immediately proc Sap Magic on your follow-up attack to heal the trade back. Never W into him while his Rage bar is near full.
edits.after: Gnar owns the first three levels and you have to respect it. Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against your 525 W (Twisted Advance), so he chips you for free — and at Level 1 you have one ability and no combo. Don't walk into Q range for melee last-hits; eat the CS loss and wait. Your one real opening arrives at Levels 2-3 with W+Q+E online. His Hop is only 475, though, so a Gnar who hops at you is inside your W range: root him, Q-knockback, and proc Sap Magic on the follow-up attack, which his own spell hits have already sped up. Never W in while his Rage bar is near full.

edits.before: This is where it levels out to a skill matchup. Your W-root into Q is a real threat now, and Sap Magic heals back his boomerang poke if you can land even one trade per cooldown — but at 6 he gets Mega-Gnar, and that flips your all-in on its head. The instant you commit W, a low-Rage Gnar who transforms will AOE-stun you (Mega W) and Wallop you back, walking out of your follow-up. Watch his Rage bar like a clock: engage when it's empty and he's stuck in mini form, back off when it's full. Drop E saplings on the brush and your retreat path to deny his hop angles and zone him off free poke.
edits.after: This is where it levels out to a skill matchup. Your W-root into Q is a real threat now, and Sap Magic heals his boomerang poke back — the poke itself shortens that heal, so chip damage is not pure loss. Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight, so nothing he throws into the dash lands; the danger is after arrival, when a full-Rage Gnar transforms, Wallops you and walks out of the follow-up. Watch his Rage bar like a clock: engage on empty, back off on full. Drop E saplings on the brush and your retreat path to deny his hop angles.

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Rage Gnar' in mid as a probable wrong ability name for 'Rage Gene'. It is a false positive — the phrase on the page is 'a low-Rage Gnar', ordinary English, not an ability name. The old mid text did contain a real error though: it said a LOW-Rage Gnar transforms when you commit, which is backwards (transformation happens at MAXIMUM Rage), and my rewrite fixes it to full-Rage. Two things I could not verify and left alone: whether Nature's Grasp terrain counts as a wall for GNAR!'s wall-stun bonus, and whether a sapling's damage counts for Rage generation. Both would be high-value if the user can confirm them.
